t: This is Cromwell Road, a major road in Kensington and Chelsea, part of the A4. It was created in the nineteenth century, and it's said to be named after Richard Cromwell, son of Oliver Cromwell, who once owned a house here. Two women are linked to the road. Clarissa Eden was born here; she later married Anthony Eden, the prime minister, and in 2007, at eighty-seven, published a memoir. Nina Boyle died here. She was a journalist and suffrage campaigner, and in April 1918 she became the first woman to submit a nomination to stand for the House of Commons.
